title: Exposed: Putin's think tank drew up secret plan to swing 2016 US election
text: It was a blueprint for meddling. A Russian government think tank controlled by Vladimir Putin drew up a plan to swing the 2016 U.S. presidential election to Donald Trump and wreck voters' faith in the American electoral system, according to three current and four former U.S. officials. They described two confidential documents from the think tank as the framework and rationale for what U.S. intelligence agencies have concluded was an intensive Russian effort to interfere with the Nov. 8 election. U.S. intelligence officials got hold of the documents, prepared by the Moscow-based Russian Institute for Strategic Studies, after the election. And who runs the institute? Retired senior Russian foreign intelligence officials appointed by Putin's office. The first document was a strategy paper written last June. It circulated at the very highest levels of the Russian government, though it was not addressed to any specific individuals. Its recommendation was chilling: the Kremlin should launch a propaganda campaign on social media and Russian state-backed global news outlets to push U.S. voters to elect a president who would take a softer line on Russia than the administration of then-President Barack Obama, the seven officials said. A second document, drafted in October and distributed the same way, warned that Democratic candidate Hillary Clinton was likely to win. So what was the new plan? Russia should drop its pro-Trump propaganda and ramp up its messaging about voter fraud, to undermine the U.S. electoral system's legitimacy and damage Clinton's reputation in an effort to undermine her presidency, the seven officials said. The officials spoke on condition of anonymity because the Russian documents are classified. They refused to discuss how the United States obtained them. U.S. intelligence agencies also declined to comment.

title: Iran got its nuclear deal. Now it must free Jason Rezaian!
text: Just as negotiators were finishing a deal on Iran's nuclear program on Monday, Post reporter Jason Rezaian was hauled back into a Tehran court for yet another session of his secret, irregular and blatantly political trial. A coincidence? We find that hard to believe. Mr. Rezaian, a 39-year-old California native arrested just under a year ago, has been cruelly dragged into a supporting role in the long negotiations between Tehran and a U.S.-led coalition. He is a pawn, used by hard-liners to sabotage goodwill, or perhaps to show that any accord Iran strikes with the West will not change its repressive domestic regime or its anti-Western policies. His ordeal has inflicted untold physical and psychological suffering on a journalist who moved to Iran hoping to improve Americans' understanding of its people and culture. Enough is enough! Now that the nuclear deal is done, it is long past time for Iranian authorities to free Mr. Rezaian, along with two and possibly three other Americans imprisoned in the country, including pastor Saeed Abedini and retired U.S. Marine Amir Hekmati. President Obama and Secretary of State John F. Kerry have talked hopefully of charting a new course in relations between the countries. If that is ever going to happen, freeing the prisoners must come first. Mohammad Javad Zarif, the Iranian foreign minister who has also hinted at a new era of cooperation, ought to understand this. He has called Mr. Rezaian a "friend" and "a good reporter"; he clearly knows there is no basis for the espionage charges against him. Yet during the negotiations, Mr. Zarif dodged questions about the Post reporter, and at one point even suggested, absurdly, that he might have been duped into wrongdoing.

title: The humble safety pin becomes a powerful symbol of defiance after Trump's win
text: The presidential election set off a wave of political accessorizing, with hats and more, as passionate voters wore their positions on their sleeves (or heads or chests). And the post-election mood suggests the trend is not slowing down. The hottest new political fashion statement? The safety pin, already embraced in the past by celebrities (remember Elizabeth Hurley's Versace dress?) and by the punk movement. After the election of Donald J. Trump, fears are mounting that parts of his base may physically or emotionally abuse minorities, immigrants, women and members of the L.G.B.T. community. In a striking show of support, people all across America are fastening safety pins to their lapels, shirts and dresses to signal that they are linked, ready to stand up for the vulnerable. “It’s a matter of showing people who get it that I will always be a resource and an ally to anyone and everyone who wants to reach out,” said Kaye Kagaoan, 24, a graphic designer from the Philippines who lives in Brooklyn. “When I saw it on Facebook, it was so simple. It resonated with me.” The stars are joining in. On Friday, the actor Patrick Stewart posted a photo of himself on Twitter wearing a pin on his jacket. The photographer Cass Bird shared an Instagram post about why she is wearing one, which opened with “If you wear a hijab, I’ll sit with you on the train” and ended with: “If you need me, I’ll be with you. All I ask is that you be with me, too.” In between, sentences began with “If you’re a person of color …” and “If you’re a refugee …” and offered different kinds of support. The actress Jaime King posted the very same words on her Instagram account. A tiny pin, a powerful message!

title: Michelle Obama says black children are not as welcome in museums as white children
text: First Lady Michelle Obama, who has led a campaign on healthy eating, has taken on a role in promoting the Obama administration's coordinated messaging on race. In a speech on Monday that was intended to celebrate the opening of a new museum, she instead deepened the racial divide that has widened during her husband's presidency. She said that museums and concert halls do not welcome non-white visitors, especially children, in the way they welcome white visitors. Speaking at the new Whitney museum in New York City's meatpacking district last week, Obama said she grew up thinking that museums were not places for someone who looks like her. She said: "You see, there are so many kids in this country who look at places like museums and concert halls and other cultural centers and they think to themselves, well, that's not a place for me, for someone who looks like me, for someone who comes from my neighborhood. In fact, I guarantee you that right now, there are kids living less than a mile from here who would never in a million years dream that they would be welcome in this museum. And growing up on the South Side of Chicago, I was one of those kids myself. So I know that feeling of not belonging in a place like this. And today, as first lady, I know how that feeling limits the horizons of far too many of our young people." According to Twitchy, the remarks received little attention outside the event until a local radio host reported on them under the heading Museums as White Spaces. The first lady is not expected to address that question in the near future.

title: Deal or no deal? Kerry admits he can't say if Iran agreement is within reach
text: On the eve of crucial new talks with Iran, U.S. Secretary of State John Kerry made a stark admission: he does not know whether an interim agreement on Iran's nuclear program is within reach. "I can't tell you whether or not we can get a deal, whether we are close," Kerry told a news conference on Saturday in the Red Sea resort of Sharm el-Sheik, where he was attending an Egyptian investment summit. "The purpose of these negotiations is not just to get a deal, it is to get the right deal," he added. The United States and five other major powers, Britain, Germany, France, China and Russia, will resume negotiations with Iran in Lausanne, Switzerland, from Sunday. The goal: a framework agreement by the end of the month. Then the two sides would try to negotiate by June 30 a final agreement curbing Iran's most sensitive nuclear activities for at least 10 years, with sanctions on the Islamic Republic gradually lifted in return. But a cloud hangs over the talks. Kerry again voiced concern that last week's letter to Iran from Republican senators may have undermined them. The letter warned Iran that any deal made by President Barack Obama might last only as long as he stayed in office, a highly unusual intervention in U.S. foreign policy-making. Kerry said he would assure Iranian negotiators and European allies at the upcoming talks that Congress did not have the authority to change the deal. "As far as we're concerned, Congress has no ability to change an executive agreement," Kerry said, adding that "important gaps" still remained between the sides. The letter came hot on the heels of a speech to Congress earlier this month by Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, who warned that Obama was negotiating a "bad deal" with Iran.

title: Trump responds with sarcasm after supporter calls President Obama a Muslim
text: Another incident of this kind has occurred. A supporter of Donald Trump shouted at a Trump rally in New Hampshire on Tuesday that President Obama was a Muslim. On this occasion, Trump's only response was a sarcastic reply, which in effect signalled to his supporters that racism is acceptable as a source of humour. In the reply, Trump pretended to rebuke the supporter for the hateful comment: "Oh, I'm supposed to reprimand the man. Who was the man that said that? I have to reprimand. How dare you. Okay, I reprimanded him. I reprimanded him, now the press can't be angry." The response was not unexpected. Trump's campaign is no longer taken seriously, to the point that describing it as a joke has become repetitive, and the same applies to the media. Even when Trump uses hateful rhetoric, the media respond with amusement, and the incidents no longer cause shock. The incident was not humorous. When CNN reported on it, its presenters smiled, and a photograph of the broadcast shows their reaction to the incident. The situation appears increasingly unreal. The underlying reason is that hateful content attracts audiences. Trump benefits the media, and the media in turn benefit him. Trump was accurate when he said that he was good for business: low-cost reality television and political theatre, including calling the president a Muslim, are treated as entertainment.

title: Video shows Giuliani anticipated FBI letter two days before its release
text: A recently reviewed video raises serious questions about how former New York City Mayor Rudy Giuliani knew that information damaging to Hillary Clinton would be released, exactly two days before it happened. Appearing on Fox News on October 26, Giuliani was confident that something would be released. Smiling broadly, he said: "I think he's got a surprise or two that you're gonna hear about in the next few days." Two days later, FBI Director James Comey released his letter to Congress setting out unspecified information regarding emails and Hillary Clinton. Giuliani is Comey's former superior, and it appears that the former New York mayor received information before anyone else. This would establish that the Hatch Act was violated, and Giuliani would be part of the violation. According to CNN: "Congress passed the Hatch Act in response to concerns that federal employees had been used to support candidates during the 1938 congressional elections. Its general intent is to greatly restrict the ability of most federal employees to engage in political campaign activities (such as soliciting campaign donations or actively working on behalf of individual candidates), especially while on the job or to otherwise use [their] official authority or influence for the purpose of interfering with or affecting the result of an election." Giuliani is one of Republican presidential candidate Donald Trump's leading surrogates on the campaign trail, and he appeared to know about information that would directly harm Trump's opponent days before it was released. He knew something. It is not known what he knew or how he obtained the information.

title: John McCain's son responds to racist criticism of Old Navy advertisement
text: After racist critics complained about an Old Navy advertisement featuring an interracial couple, Senator John McCain's son responded to them. The advertisement had been posted by Old Navy on April 29, 2016, promoting 30% off customers' entire purchase. McCain's son Jack is a Navy lieutenant and is married to Air Force Reserve Captain Renee Swift, who is black. When racist critics attacked interracial marriage on Friday, Jack McCain took the matter personally. In response, he wrote on Twitter, telling the critics in strong terms to stop. "To the people upset about the #OldNavy Scandal of an a picture of a mixed race marriage, eat it." McCain wrote on May 2, 2016, alongside a picture of the couple. He then posted a picture of the two of them on their wedding day, writing: "I hope this one burns too, you ignorant racists. Here is us on our wedding day." McCain received a large amount of support on his Twitter account, including from CNN anchor Jake Tapper, who wrote that "anyone who has a problem with it is an idiot clinging to a backward time." McCain's posts appear to have affected the racist critics, because some of them responded with offensive replies, including one that read: "No, you're not."

title: Report says Comey statement was false and FBI searched Weiner laptop under misused terror warrant
text: Comey's account was false: the FBI used a prohibited FISA domestic terror warrant in the search for Clinton emails on Anthony Weiner's laptop, creating a constitutional crisis. In an unexpected announcement, the Department of Justice admitted that there was no legal authorization in place to access the email accounts of Hillary Clinton aide Huma Abedin, the estranged wife of former Congressman Anthony Weiner, who has been accused of sex offences. The government admitted that no warrant had been requested and that discussions to seek one had not yet begun. This makes the letter FBI Director James Comey sent to Congress on Friday a potentially criminal act, if it can be proven that Comey was aware of this and of his subordinates' actions in "planting" Clinton emails on Weiner's laptop, which the FBI "synced". CNN reported: "Justice Department and FBI officials are working to secure approval that would allow the FBI to conduct a full search of top Hillary Clinton aide Huma Abedin's newly discovered emails, sources familiar with the discussions said. Government lawyers haven't yet approached Abedin's lawyers to seek an agreement to conduct the search. Sources earlier said that those discussions had begun, but the law enforcement officials now say they have not." Comey is facing strong criticism for conduct that is seen as more than partisan. Former presidential adviser Lanny Davis wrote in The Hill: “Comey as FBI director — an investigative agency, not a prosecution agency — (does not) have any authority to send a report to Congress in the middle of an investigation about the past or present subject of an investigation.”

title: Journalists report hostility from Trump supporters at rallies
text: Journalists across the country are complaining about the treatment members of the press receive at Trump campaign rallies from Trump supporters, whom the media routinely misrepresent as ignorant racists, fascists or disaffected white workers. Increasingly often, these journalists are "reporting" that they are victims of Trump supporters who chant phrases such as "CNN sucks" and call them names such as "presstitutes." For members of the established media, the occasional taunts and jeers represent a dangerous threat to press freedom. In an interview with Kellyanne Conway on Tuesday, CNN's Wolf Blitzer asked Trump's campaign manager to ask Trump to stop criticising the press at his rallies, because he was concerned "there could be an ugly incident" between Trump supporters and the "hardworking young journalists" who cover the rallies. A review of media stories from the last two weeks found more than a dozen articles in major publications with the same "journalists victimized by Trump supporters at rallies" narrative. Trump supporters endure long waits, difficult parking and often seats with obstructed views to attend rallies for their candidate. The press, by contrast, is given a separate entrance, reserved seating and protection from event security and the Secret Service. An extensive search by this reporter found no incidents of members of the media being physically attacked or assaulted at Trump rallies. This has not prevented the inaccurate characterization of Trump supporters as creating a "menacing" and "dangerous" environment for journalists. The narrative first appeared briefly in August, when NBC's Katy Tur wrote a long article in Marie Claire describing her confrontational relationship with Trump and the reaction among his supporters to his "insults" about her reporting.

title: Trump criticizes Obamacare and cites economic gains in Monday morning tweets
text: Donald Trump is focused on undoing President Obama's achievements and on taking credit for them. In a series of Twitter posts on Monday morning, July 31, 2017, Trump first criticized the Affordable Care Act. He wrote: "If ObamaCare is hurting people, & it is, why shouldn't it hurt the insurance companies & why should Congress not be paying what public pays?" Trump's statement is false. Members of Congress must buy health insurance through the exchanges like other Americans, and they do not receive a special subsidy. They pay what other Americans pay. According to FactCheck.org, lawmakers and their staffs face additional requirements that other Americans do not, and the subsidy that Trump appears to be referring to is a contribution from the federal government. Lawmakers receive a contribution from their employer, as do ordinary Americans who get insurance through their employer. However, lawmakers no longer get insurance through their employer as they once did. Members of Congress previously had their health care paid for by taxpayers. That arrangement ended under Obamacare, when lawmakers were required to buy a private plan through the exchanges like everyone else. In other words, Congress pays what the public pays. Trump then again took credit for the economy that President Obama oversaw. He wrote: "Highest Stock Market EVER, best economic numbers in years, unemployment lowest in 17 years, wages raising, border secure, S.C.: No WH chaos!" By the end of President Obama's tenure, and well before Trump was elected, the stock market had already reached record highs. Unemployment fell to under 5 percent as a result of Obama's record 75 consecutive months of job growth. Wages also rose by 2.9 percent.

title: Bali in terror: nearly 135,000 flee as Mount Agung threatens to blow
text: An island in fear. Nearly 135,000 people on the Indonesian island of Bali have abandoned their homes and crammed into makeshift evacuation centers after warnings that the Mount Agung volcano could erupt at any moment, officials said late on Thursday. Spewing white smoke and sending tremors rippling through the area, Mount Agung had its alert status raised to the highest level last week. Since then, tens of thousands of villagers have fled their homes beneath the menacing volcano. The national disaster management agency said many people have run because they are unsure how close they are to a 12 km (seven miles) exclusion zone imposed around the crater. Evacuees are now packed into tents, school gyms and government buildings in neighboring villages. Food, water, medicines and other supplies are plentiful, but the evacuees dread a long, agonizing wait that could wreck their livelihoods. One farmer is terrified that lava flows could wipe out his house and farm. "If my house is destroyed I don't know how to restart my life. I don't know where my kids will sleep and all I can do now is pray," said Gusti Gege Astana, 40. Heartbreaking. Officials also noted that around 30,000 cattle are trapped within the danger zone around the volcano, and efforts are under way to move the livestock, a vital source of income for many residents. And the past is chilling: more than 1,000 people were killed the last time Mount Agung erupted, in 1963. Will history repeat itself? An elderly woman who survived that disaster said evacuation orders had come much earlier this time. "Back then we weren't evacuated until it got really dangerous. Life went on as normal when ash and gravel was falling on us, until the big lava came out and destroyed everything," said 82-year-old Gusti Ayu Wati.

title: Two Iowa police officers shot and killed in separate attacks; search for suspect under way
text: Early on Wednesday morning, two Iowa police officers were shot and killed in two separate ambush-style attacks. Police from the Urbandale and Des Moines departments responded to a report of gunfire at the intersection of 70th Street and Aurora Avenue at approximately 1:06 a.m., according to the Des Moines Register. Officers have not yet identified a suspect or suspects in the shootings and have not identified the officers who were killed. One unnamed officer was found dead by fellow officers in Urbandale, at the intersection of 70th Street, according to a press conference given by Police Sgt. Paul Parizek. A second officer was then found in Des Moines, on Merle Hay Road. Both roads and the surrounding roads have been closed. Both officers were shot in their squad cars. Video has emerged of one of the crime scenes, at 70th Street and Aurora Avenue, the scene of the first shooting, where an officer was found shot early on Wednesday morning. Some officers at the scene were wearing combat gear. Police Sgt. Paul Parizek addressed the press and the residents of Iowa, stating that there is a clear and present danger for police officers. He said he believes the shootings were targeted. “There’s literally a clear and present danger if you’re a police officer,” Parizek said. “I don’t even know where to begin on how bad this year is but this is what we do. We come in day in and day out, we go out there and provide the same level of service regardless of what’s going on in our personal and professional lives.” Parizek added. Iowa Gov. Terry Branstad released a statement on Wednesday morning. A manhunt is under way.

title: Trump's white women problem is brutal: 'You just want to smack him'
text: The clock is ticking! With just five weeks of campaigning left, Hillary Clinton and Donald Trump are scrambling desperately to win over female voters in America's suburbs, where well-educated white women have emerged as perhaps the most pivotal swing group of the whole presidential race. Can he possibly win them back?

title: Putin says Russia is ready to restore relations with the United States
text: Russian President Vladimir Putin said that Russia is ready and looks forward to restoring bilateral relations with the United States, commenting on the news of Donald Trump's victory in the US presidential election. “We heard [Trump's] campaign rhetoric while still a candidate for the US presidency, which was focused on restoring the relations between Russia and the United States,” Putin said, speaking at a ceremony in Moscow at which foreign ambassadors presented their letters of credentials. “We understand and are aware that it will be a difficult path in the light of the degradation in which, unfortunately, the relationship between Russia and the US are at the moment,” he added. Referring to the degraded state of relations between the two countries, Putin again stressed that “it is not our fault that Russia-US relations are as you see them.” Earlier in the day, in a message to Donald Trump, the Russian president expressed confidence that dialogue between Moscow and Washington, in keeping with each other's views, meets the interests of both Russia and the United States. In the message, Putin said he hopes to address some “burning issues that are currently on the international agenda, and search for effective responses to the challenges of the global security,” RIA Novosti reported. Putin also expressed confidence that “building a constructive dialogue between Moscow and Washington, based on principles of equality, mutual respect and each other's positions, meets the interests of the peoples of our countries and of the entire international community.” Russian State Duma Speaker Vyacheslav Volodin also expressed hope that Trump's victory in the presidential election will help prepare the way for a more constructive dialogue between Moscow and Washington. “The current US-Russian relations cannot be called friendly.”

title: Hollywood titan Harvey Weinstein forced out on indefinite leave as harassment scandal explodes
text: A Hollywood giant stumbles! The Weinstein Company board of representatives said in a statement that it takes “extremely seriously” the shocking accusations in the Times story, which said Weinstein had made eight settlements with women who accused him of unwanted physical contact and sexual harassment over three decades. Three decades! Meanwhile, the Democratic National Committee (DNC) and several Democratic politicians, including Senators Kamala Harris, Cory Booker and Chuck Schumer, said on Friday they will redirect Weinstein's political donations to women's rights groups. title: Bombshell move: Virginia governor hands voting rights back to 200,000 felons
text: A dramatic power play! Gov. Terry McAuliffe of Virginia used his executive power on Friday to restore voting rights to more than 200,000 convicted felons, going straight around the legislature. The action effectively overturns a Civil provision in the state's Constitution that, he said, was aimed at disenfranchising. And the stakes are huge. The sweeping order, in a swing state that could help decide the November presidential election, will allow all felons who have served their prison time and finished parole or probation to register to vote. Nearly half are a core constituency of Democrats, Mr. McAuliffe's own party. Coincidence? Amid intensifying national attention over harsh sentencing policies with disproportionate effects, governors and legislatures around the nation have been debating, and often battling over, moves to restore voting rights for convicted felons. Virginia imposes especially harsh restrictions, barring felons from voting for life. In Kentucky, Gov. Matt Bevin, a newly elected Republican, recently tore up an order enacted by his Democratic predecessor that was similar to the one Mr. McAuliffe signed Friday. In Maryland, Gov. Larry Hogan, a Republican, vetoed a measure to restore voting rights to convicted felons, but Democrats in the state legislature overrode him in February, and an estimated 44,000 former prisoners who are on probation can now register to vote. “There’s no question that we’ve had a horrible history in voting rights as relates to — we should remedy it,” Mr. McAuliffe said in an interview Thursday, previewing the announcement he made on the steps of Virginia's Capitol, just yards from where President Abraham Lincoln once addressed freed slaves. “We should do it as soon as we possibly can.” Republicans in the Virginia Legislature have fought measures to expand voting rights for convicted felons.

title: Obamacare repeal collapses, and now nervous insurers are demanding answers on subsidies
text: The chaos deepens. A failed Republican push to replace Obamacare sparked fresh alarm on Tuesday among U.S. health insurers over whether the government will keep funding billions of dollars in medical benefit subsidies. The healthcare bill in the U.S. Senate would have settled the funding question, but it was scrapped after Republican leaders could not round up enough party members to pass it. Its collapse will test whether Republicans and Democrats can stabilize an insurance market serving some 10 million Americans in time for 2018. Can they? Republican President Donald Trump has hinted several times that he could kill the so-called cost-sharing reduction subsidies, which help pay consumers' out-of-pocket healthcare costs. The administration could do so as early as August. Insurers have braced for the worst, in many cases hiking proposed premium prices for 2018 by more than 20 percent to cover the lost funding. On Tuesday, insurers said they want Congress to appropriate the money for these payments. If that does not happen, and the Trump administration moves further to undermine Democratic former President Barack Obama's healthcare law, more insurers may flee markets for next year ahead of a late September deadline. That could force consumers to switch plans or insurers, or leave them with no options at all! “Our members and all Americans need the certainty and security of knowing coverage will be available and affordable for them,” said Justine Handelman, senior vice president in the Office of Policy and Representation at the Blue Cross Blue Shield Association, which represents insurers nationwide. “We have consistently urged that there be immediate, certain funding for the cost-sharing reduction program, which helps those most in need with out-of-pocket costs when they access medical care.”

title: Funny or Die releases Donald Trump film starring Johnny Depp
text: On the morning after Donald Trump's large win in the New Hampshire primary, it was revealed that the comedy website Funny or Die has made a Donald Trump movie starring Johnny Depp, which it had been working on for months. The film is a TV movie adaptation of Trump's bestseller The Art of the Deal, and its title is Funny Or Die Presents Donald Trump's The Art Of The Deal: The Movie. In effect, it is a Trump movie from the 1980s. On Wednesday the humor website began streaming the 50-minute comedy, in which Mr. Depp portrays the businessman turned politician, including a full comb-over. The film was kept secret for months, which is difficult in Hollywood, and was released to coincide with Mr. Trump's victory on Tuesday in the New Hampshire Republican presidential primary. "It was a crazy, completely nuts idea that somehow we pulled off," said Adam McKay, a co-founder of Funny or Die. Will Ferrell and Judd Apatow are also principal partners in the site, which produces exclusive material that often features well-known stars. Mr. McKay is the director of The Big Short, which is a contender for best picture at the coming Academy Awards, and he also commented on the site's newest satire of Mr. Trump.

title: Trump's wild convention lineup: Ivanka, Newt, a UFC boss and a whole lot of family
text: Expect the unexpected! The roster of speakers at the convention that will officially crown Donald Trump is a colorful grab bag of political leaders, entertainers, personalities and the candidate's own family, perfectly in keeping with his campaign's unorthodox style. The presumptive GOP nominee's wife, Melania Trump, takes the stage Monday, the convention's opening night. Daughter Tiffany Trump and son Donald Trump Jr. will address the convention Tuesday evening. Trump's younger son, Eric, speaks Wednesday. Thursday's program features daughter Ivanka Trump, a key player in her father's inner circle, followed by the big moment: the billionaire businessman's speech Thursday night accepting the GOP nomination. Brand-new Trump running mate Mike Pence speaks on Wednesday evening. And what about Tebow? "I wake up this morning to find out that I'm speaking at the Republican National Convention," Tebow said. "It's amazing how fast rumors fly and that's exactly what it is -- a rumor." Each night of the four-night gathering in Cleveland will center on a different theme, such as security, immigration and the economy. The first night will hammer security and immigration, with discussions of the Benghazi attack and the U.S. border. Speakers include Jamiel Shaw, whose son was killed by an undocumented immigrant, and Cotton. Sen. Joni Ernst of Iowa, the first female combat veteran elected to the Senate, will also speak, as will Rep. Ryan Zinke, a former Navy Seal. Benghazi attack survivors Mark Geist and John Tiegen will also speak Monday night. A late Monday addition: Pastor Mark Burns, a prominent African American evangelical leader, Bloomberg reported Sunday. On the second night, speakers will zero in on the economy, with presenters including Dana White, the UFC president.
